short_summary: This dissertation consists of three empirical papers in applied microeconomics.Although the topics differ, firms' adjustment to macro shock, environmental effects of trade, and historical elite persistence, the common methodological approach is to exploit plausibly exogenous variation to study long-run adjustment at the firm, regional, and family levels.Each chapter examines how economic agents respond to external shocks that are largely outside their immediate control, allowing for causal inference on structural transformation, air quality change, and intergenerational correlation.Large excha
